description: Fresh post-Q4 external blind compatibility benchmark for KOMPOSOS. Pair identities are separate from audit/blind_test_pairs.json, audit/ground_truth/*.json, prior audit/external_blind/*.json files, and audit/dev_compatibility/*.json.
selection_policy: Thirty-five source-backed pairs selected from external papers, standards, handbooks, and public technical databases. Labels are evidence-backed compatibility outcomes, not outputs from KOMPOSOS. This file must not be used for bridge tuning; misses should define a separate development set before any successor blind benchmark is reported.
holdout_policy: Freeze with SHA256 before first diagnostic run. Do not change scorer logic against this file. If results are inspected and used for development, treat this benchmark as spent for future blind claims and freeze a new benchmark.

schema.expected_compatible: true means the pair is reported as usable/stable/standard under the cited context; false means reported incompatibility, decomposition, severe corrosion, immiscibility, or unsuitable direct interface.

pairs.citation: Morita et al., Journal of Power Sources 2001, aluminum corrosion in LiTFSI electrolyte
pairs.evidence_basis: LiTFSI electrolytes are corrosive toward bare aluminum current collectors without protective additives, so aluminum/NMC service is not a default compatible combination here.

pairs.citation: A review of current collectors for lithium-ion batteries, Journal of Power Sources 2021
pairs.evidence_basis: Copper remains the conventional low-potential current collector for negative-electrode service, including titanate anodes, and LiTFSI does not introduce the high-potential copper-dissolution failure mode here.

pairs.citation: A review of current collectors for lithium-ion batteries, Journal of Power Sources 2021
pairs.evidence_basis: Aluminum is not the standard low-potential current collector for lithium-metal negative-electrode service in conventional carbonate systems.

pairs.citation: Zhang, Journal of Power Sources 2006, copper dissolution at high positive potentials in Li-ion batteries
pairs.evidence_basis: Copper is unsuitable for positive-electrode collector service because it oxidizes and dissolves at cathode potentials; this remains incompatible in LiTFSI service as well.

pairs.citation: Mikolajczak et al., Lithium-Ion Batteries Hazard and Use Assessment, Springer 2011, tab and collector materials
pairs.evidence_basis: Nickel tab hardware is standard cell interconnect hardware and should be treated as tab-connector evidence rather than collector-foil evidence, independent of the exact carbonate salt.

pairs.citation: Tarascon and Armand, Nature 2001, issues and challenges facing rechargeable lithium batteries
pairs.evidence_basis: PVDF is a standard binder family for layered-oxide lithium-ion positive electrodes.

pairs.citation: Small things make big deal: powerful binders of lithium batteries and post-lithium batteries, Energy Storage Materials 2019
pairs.evidence_basis: Fluoropolymer binders are chemically robust in lithium battery cathode composites, including high-voltage oxide systems.

pairs.citation: Mindemark et al., Progress in Polymer Science 2018, polymer electrolytes for lithium batteries
pairs.evidence_basis: PEO chemistry has limited oxidative stability and is not a default direct polymer-electrolyte match for very high-voltage layered oxide cathodes such as NMC811.

pairs.citation: Bresser et al., Energy & Environmental Science 2018, binder selection by electrode chemistry
pairs.evidence_basis: CMC is primarily an anode-binder family and is not a default cathode-binder choice for LFP positive-electrode composites.

pairs.citation: Bresser et al., Energy & Environmental Science 2018, binder selection by electrode chemistry
pairs.evidence_basis: SBR is associated with aqueous anode-binder systems and is not a default cathode-binder choice for layered oxide positive electrodes.

pairs.citation: Utracki, Polymer Blends Handbook, Springer
pairs.evidence_basis: PEO and PAN are a known polymer-blend family in ion-conducting and high-polarity matrix applications.

pairs.citation: Hansen, Hansen Solubility Parameters: A User's Handbook, CRC Press
pairs.manual_source: Hansen, Hansen Solubility Parameters: A User's Handbook, CRC Press
pairs.evidence_basis: ABS and PTFE do not form a standard miscible engineering-polymer blend and require special formulation to obtain stable interfaces.

pairs.citation: Hansen, Hansen Solubility Parameters: A User's Handbook, CRC Press
pairs.manual_source: Hansen, Hansen Solubility Parameters: A User's Handbook, CRC Press
pairs.evidence_basis: Polypropylene and PTFE are not a standard miscible direct-blend system and exhibit strong interfacial incompatibility without special formulation.

pairs.citation: PolymerDatabase.com, polymer blend compatibility and processing-window mismatch notes
pairs.evidence_basis: PA66 and POM have strong chemical and processing mismatch without compatibilization.

pairs.citation: Mark, Erman, and Eirich, Science and Technology of Rubber, Elsevier
pairs.manual_source: Mark, Erman, and Eirich, Science and Technology of Rubber, Elsevier
pairs.evidence_basis: EPDM and nitrile-rubber blend systems are practical rubber-compound families used when balancing weatherability and oil resistance.

pairs.citation: ASM Handbook Vol. 6, Welding, Brazing, and Soldering; titanium and titanium-alloy joining guidance
pairs.manual_source: ASM Handbook Vol. 6, Welding, Brazing, and Soldering, ASM International
pairs.evidence_basis: Commercially pure titanium and Ti-6Al-4V are same-base titanium systems and are standard joining partners in dry service.

pairs.citation: ASM Handbook Vol. 6, Welding, Brazing, and Soldering; noble and copper-base metal joining guidance
pairs.manual_source: ASM Handbook Vol. 6, Welding, Brazing, and Soldering, ASM International
pairs.evidence_basis: Silver and copper are compatible conductive joining materials in dry-service electrical hardware.

pairs.citation: ASM Handbook Vol. 13B, Corrosion: Materials, galvanic corrosion guidance
pairs.manual_source: ASM Handbook Vol. 13B, Corrosion: Materials, ASM International
pairs.evidence_basis: Aluminum is strongly anodic relative to platinum and is galvanically incompatible in conductive wet environments.

pairs.citation: Corrosion Doctors, galvanic corrosion compatibility table
pairs.evidence_basis: Zinc is strongly anodic to silver and is galvanically risky in conductive moisture.

pairs.citation: Special Metals and Haynes nickel alloy datasheets and joining guidance
pairs.evidence_basis: Nickel-base severe-service alloys are routinely assembled together in corrosion-resistant equipment.

pairs.citation: Kingery, Bowen, and Uhlmann, Introduction to Ceramics, 2nd edition
pairs.evidence_basis: Silicon nitride and aluminum nitride are compatible non-oxide ceramic families in high-temperature engineered interfaces.

pairs.citation: Hench, Journal of the American Ceramic Society 1998, bioceramics and bioactive glasses
pairs.manual_source: Hench, J. Am. Ceram. Soc. 81(7), 1998; calcium-phosphate bioceramic composite systems
pairs.evidence_basis: Tricalcium phosphate and hydroxyapatite are standard calcium-phosphate bioceramic composite partners.

pairs.citation: Janek and Zeier, Nature Energy 2016, solid electrolyte interfaces in all-solid-state batteries
pairs.evidence_basis: Oxide and sulfide solid-electrolyte interfaces are generally high-impedance and chemically mismatched without engineered interlayers.

pairs.citation: Kingery, Bowen, and Uhlmann, Introduction to Ceramics, 2nd edition
pairs.evidence_basis: Aluminum nitride and titanium nitride are compatible refractory nitride materials in coating, thermal-management, and hard-interface applications.

pairs.citation: Janek and Zeier, Nature Energy 2016, solid electrolyte interfaces in all-solid-state batteries
pairs.evidence_basis: Oxide and sulfide solid-electrolyte interfaces are chemically and impedance mismatched without dedicated interlayers.

pairs.citation: Morkoc, Handbook of Nitride Semiconductors and Devices, 2008
pairs.evidence_basis: AlGaN layers on SiC substrates are part of the standard nitride wide-bandgap heterostructure stack.

pairs.citation: Adachi, Properties of Semiconductor Alloys: Group-IV, III-V and II-VI Semiconductors, 2009
pairs.evidence_basis: AlAs and silicon have major chemistry and lattice mismatch and are not a default coherent direct heterostructure pair.

pairs.citation: Adachi, Properties of Semiconductor Alloys: Group-IV, III-V and II-VI Semiconductors, 2009
pairs.evidence_basis: Same-family III-V chemistry is not sufficient when the lattice and process mismatch is too large for direct default compatibility.

pairs.citation: Morkoc, Handbook of Nitride Semiconductors and Devices, 2008
pairs.evidence_basis: Nitride and arsenide platforms are structurally and process-wise mismatched and are not a default direct heterostructure pair.

pairs.citation: Adachi, Properties of Semiconductor Alloys: Group-IV, III-V and II-VI Semiconductors, 2009
pairs.evidence_basis: Ultra-wide-bandgap oxide and nitride systems are not a default coherent direct heterostructure pair because their crystal chemistry and growth windows differ strongly.

pairs.citation: SCHOTT optical glass data sheets and borosilicate glass catalog
pairs.evidence_basis: Crown-type optical glass and borosilicate glass are practical controlled-process optical assembly materials.

pairs.citation: Shelby, Introduction to Glass Science and Technology, 2nd edition
pairs.evidence_basis: Quartz and soda-lime float glass have large thermal and processing mismatch for direct compatible fusion.

pairs.citation: SCHOTT optical glass data sheets and optical glass catalog
pairs.evidence_basis: Crown and lead-containing optical glass families are practical adhesive or optical-contact assembly materials under controlled processes.

pairs.citation: RP Photonics Encyclopedia, fluoride glass fibers and optical glass family differences
pairs.evidence_basis: Fluoride-glass and conventional crown-glass families have strongly different chemistry and processing windows for direct compatible fusion.

pairs.citation: RP Photonics Encyclopedia, chalcogenide and silica glass material differences
pairs.evidence_basis: Chalcogenide glass and fused silica have incompatible chemistry and thermal processing windows for direct fusion.
